validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification -- keep as a real, correctly classified gas transmission expansion project.
validity.researcher_notes: Real, FERC-certificated project: Docket No. CP24-8-000, 189 FERC P 61,131, 'ORDER ISSUING CERTIFICATE' (issued Nov 21, 2024), authorizing Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC to modify two existing compressor stations (CS 302, Montgomery County TX; CS 343, Liberty County TX) on its Louisiana Line to add 300,000 Dth/d of new eastbound firm transportation service. Corroborated by Kinder Morgan's own project page, the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (28 releases 2018-2026, tracking this project under docket CP24-8 from Applied(2024)->Approved(2025)->Construction(2026)->Completed(2026-08)), and the Federal Register notice of the application. Correctly classified: natural gas (Fuel=Gas), interstate transmission (PipelineType=transmission) under NGA section 7(c). Not a duplicate of any other roster row -- no other P####  in the 44-row roster describes CS 302/CS 343 modifications or this docket. Two data-quality caveats found and staged separately below (Location/StartState attribution, Owner/ownership-split attribution), plus a recommended Status change (see status_reviews).

validity.recommendation: Change StartState/Province from Louisiana to Texas -- the project's physical work (both modified compressor stations) is in Texas.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records BOTH StartState/Province and EndState/Province as Louisiana. FERC order (189 FERC P 61,131) is explicit: Compressor Station 302 is in Montgomery County, Texas, and Compressor Station 343 is in Liberty County, Texas -- both are TEXAS facilities, and all of the project's physical construction/modification work takes place there. The Louisiana Line itself runs east from CS 302 (Montgomery Co., TX) and terminates in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana -- so EndState/Province=Louisiana is correct, but the start point (where the modified facilities actually are) is Texas, not Louisiana. EIA's own dataset independently corroborates this: Beg_State=TX, End_State=LA (Aug-2026 release, row 122). Two independent government sources (FERC order + EIA dataset) agree.

validity.recommendation: Change Owner1% from 100.00% (sole Kinder Morgan ownership) to the confirmed three-way split: Kinder Morgan 37.5%, ArcLight Capital Partners 37.5%, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners 25%.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records Owner1=Kinder Morgan at 100.00%, cited to a now-dead kindermorgan.com project page. This is very likely wrong: NGPL has been jointly owned by Kinder Morgan, ArcLight Capital Partners, and Brookfield Infrastructure since at least 2023. PRNewswire (2023-06-15, independent of GEM, verified) states the exact post-transaction split: ArcLight 37.5%, Brookfield Infrastructure 25%, Kinder Morgan 37.5% (operator). EIA's Aug-2026 release corroborates all three parties remain current owners (Pipeline Operator Name field literally reads 'NGPL (Kinder Morgan / Brookfield / ArcLight)'), with no evidence of a change since 2023. A 2021 Reuters story (surfaced via gem.wiki's citation list) describing an earlier Kinder Morgan/Brookfield stake sale could not be verified (HTTP 401) and is not relied on here; the PRNewswire release + EIA dataset (2 independent, verified origins) are sufficient to establish the current value is wrong and to name the corrected split.

Two independent origins (government/EIA + operator/Kinder Morgan), both dated within the last 8 months, support moving Status from 'proposed' to 'operating' and setting StartYear1=2026/StartMonth1=7 (already the sheet's recorded value, now corroborated rather than changed). Note: the same EIA release's 'Year In Service Date' column reads 2028, contradicting its own Notes text (7/10/26) -- treated as an EIA internal data-quality defect (the generic in-service-year column appears not to have been updated for this row), not evidence against the July 2026 in-service date.
